header_summary:
Efforts to standardize Bitcoin transaction inclusion proofs using wtxid have led to a comprehensive draft proposal that consolidates multiple independent formats and implementations, offering explicit validation checks, a Python reference, and extensive test vectors. The proposal addresses challenges in verifying witness data, particularly in edge cases like block 481823, and introduces measures to ensure reliable verification for both full nodes and lightweight clients, with discourse ongoing regarding proof format compatibility and zero-padding rules [Draft Proposal](https://github.com/jeanpablojp/bips/blob/witness-inclusion-proofs/bip-witness-inclusion-proofs.md), [Discussion](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/C899B11E-4971-4AAF-8BA3-81EBAFBF7739@jeanpablo.jp/T/#u#meb2b2f0670b30c170d2e4099b87537be5c558448).

The imminent threat of quantum computing has intensified debates on legacy Bitcoin coin protection, with proposals such as landmine soft forks and auction-based rescue mechanisms offering nuanced paths between freezing vulnerable outputs and leaving them exposed. These frameworks seek to balance transparency, fairness, and deterrence by enabling verifiable claims, penalizing attackers, and incentivizing proactive migration to quantum-resistant protocols [Details](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/ffd99327-f633-4e2e-bc54-cc1389ffebccn@googlegroups.com/T/#m42c65c2f95715f2c259265b3f98c68dea5dcdcd2).

A significant portion of Bitcoin's supply—over 34%—remains in outputs with exposed public keys or scripts, highlighting persistent vulnerabilities and the limitations of on-chain analysis for assessing accidental secret retention. Detailed census data and methodology are available for review, including nuanced treatment of output types such as P2TR and multi-signature scripts [UTXO Census](https://github.com/duncan0k/btc-exposure-index/blob/2a0f4b053cad2ae3dc101a4e4c154ac2b4706f25/results/975019/utxo-census-stats.json), [Method](https://snapshots.ark0.si/method.html), [Discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/how-much-btc-sits-behind-keys-or-scripts-already-on-chain-block-975-019/3088).

Technical advancements are focused on both quantum-resistant migration and proof-of-state methods, exemplified by the Adaptive Quantum Migration Protocol (AQMP v2.0), which employs knowledge-asymmetry and stateless threshold cryptography to offer efficient, secure UTXO rescue and institutional custody in a post-quantum landscape. The protocol dramatically reduces on-chain data requirements and addresses institutional key management challenges, with full technical details and reference materials available in the [published paper](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24341314) and [BIP draft](https://github.com/laudzakusuma/aqmp-protocol).

Recent security vulnerabilities have prompted the release of updated Bitcoin Core versions [31.3](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/release-31.3/) and [30.5](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/release-30.5/), with details provided in the [security advisory](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/disclose-orphan-inv-stall/) and further context available on the [advisories page](https://bitcoincore.org/en/security-advisories/) and [mailing list](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/c47ceea6-99de-41fe-a97c-928881963eccn@googlegroups.com/T/u).

Finally, improvements in proof frameworks are being explored through Merkle hashing and alternative hash functions for UTXO snapshots, leveraging efficient tools and data structures to enhance auditability and performance, with iterative development advised for scalable, full-chain proof generation [Flock](https://github.com/succinctlabs/flock), [Binius64](https://github.com/binius-zk/binius64), [Discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/a-stark-proof-of-bitcoins-utxo-set-at-block-972-500-with-circuits-proven-in-lean/3070/7).

recent_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Witness Transaction Inclusion Proofs
recent_posts.summary: - A new draft standardizes wtxid-based transaction inclusion proofs by consolidating previous approaches and validation logic.  - It introduces validation checks, two proof formats, explicit segwit activation input, and addresses Merkle branch complexities.  - Feedback is requested to improve design decisions and promote interoperability among Bitcoin applications and clients.

recent_posts.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
recent_posts.summary: - Proposals, including landmine soft forks and auctions, aim to protect legacy Bitcoin against quantum attacks.  - Transparency about which coins are quantum-safe is essential for security and informed protocol decisions.  - Collateralized auctions and clear rescue rules incentivize honest participation while deterring quantum-enabled theft.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core security advisory for an easily discoverable vulnerability
recent_posts.summary: - Two new releases address a medium severity security vulnerability and are available for supported versions.  - Users of version 29.x are strongly advised to upgrade for continued security and reliability.  - Detailed security information and advisory links are accessible for further reference and technical discussion.

recent_posts.title: 676-Byte Knowledge-Asymmetry UTXO Rescue and Stateless Lattice PQ-MPC for Legacy Supply Migration
recent_posts.summary: - AQMP v2.0 efficiently rescues legacy UTXOs using a 676-byte knowledge-asymmetry approach, reducing on-chain burden.  - The protocol introduces a stateless threshold engine with deterministic signature generation, enhancing institutional custody security.  - Comprehensive technical materials are available, and feedback is invited on chain-code security and mempool protection.

recent_posts.title: Post Quantum Recovery Framework
recent_posts.summary: - Almost 35% of all unspent Bitcoin is protected by secrets already revealed or exposed on chain.  - The majority, around 64%, remains protected by secrets not yet revealed through any on-chain mechanism.  - The census cannot detect off-chain secret disclosure or segment outputs by age or Bitcoin era.

recent_posts.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
recent_posts.summary: - Switching to blake2s increases complexity, but publishing Merkle hashes improves verification and trust.  - Handling large data volumes requires efficient, purpose-built provers and modified data structures for auditability.  - Performance can be improved using optimized frameworks and by incrementally refining proofs from manageable snapshots.

active_posts.title: Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
active_posts.summary: - The BIP Editors processed hundreds of pull requests, published forty-two BIPs, and revitalized participation.  - Key improvements included a new BIP Process, document updates, and automation script enhancements.  - A refreshed three-member editor team is proposed to ensure sustained progress and shared responsibilities.

active_posts.title: SHRINCS: an efficient hash-based signature scheme for Bitcoin (first draft)
active_posts.summary: - SHRINCS is a proposed hash-based signature scheme offering compact keys and faster verification speeds.  - The scheme requires careful state management and computationally intensive signing, with known implementation limitations.  - Community feedback and peer review are encouraged to refine SHRINCS' cryptography, security, and compatibility features.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal introduces an optional peer-to-peer system for nodes to share stale block information.  - Stale block detection is vital for diagnosing issues like network partitions and adversarial mining strategies.  - Technical specifications restrict information sharing to recent tips, use compression, and enforce cache size limits.

active_posts.title: Unspendable keys in descriptors
active_posts.summary: - Integrating miniscript with taproot enables new wallet designs but presents challenges for unspendable key creation.  - Multiple methods for generating unspendable keys exist, each with advantages and drawbacks regarding security and usability.  - The recycling entropy approach is promising for wallet policies, but widespread standard adoption remains uncertain.

active_posts.title: Bounds on chain length with BIP-54 timewarp fixes
active_posts.summary: - New Bitcoin rules limit timestamp manipulation to prevent attacks like ArtForz and Murch-Zawy.  - A mathematical model provides an upper bound for blockchain length based on timestamps and work.  - Formal proof confirms these rules secure chain growth, aiding developers and researchers in blockchain security.

active_posts.title: SHRINCS: 324-byte stateful post-quantum signatures with static backups
active_posts.summary: - SHRINCS combines efficient stateful hash-based signatures with robust stateless ones for flexible security.  - An unbalanced XMSS tree and SPHINCS+ variant optimize efficiency and support seamless dual-mode operations.  - The scheme enables secure fallback to stateless signatures if the state is lost or corrupted.

today_in_history_posts.title: HTLC output aggregation as a mitigation for tx recycling, jamming, and on-chain efficiency (covenants)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - A security concern was raised about the lack of a revoked state broadcast in the Eltoo protocol.  - Johan requested clarification on possible exploitation and practical examples illustrating the potential risks involved.  - He emphasized the challenges of managing growing state combinations and sought efficient solutions to address them.

today_in_history_posts.title: Liquidity Ads and griefing subtleties
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Liquidity ads introduce pricing challenges and potential risks for both buyers and sellers in protocol design.  - Proposed solutions, including CLTV and splicing, present new complexities and opportunities for exploitation.  - Sellers should carefully assess risks and adjust rates, as liquidity marketplaces evolve within the ecosystem.

today_in_history_posts.title: Optimistic mining tip (slow block propagation)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Optimistic mining allows miners to begin work on a new chain tip before full validation.  - This reduces delays and could decrease the number of orphan blocks, improving overall mining efficiency.  - Block headers offer security, and if validation fails, miners revert to the previous chain tip.
